answer:
Under U.S. Rule 6c-11, an ETF may rely on the rule only if it has written agreements with each authorized participant (AP) covering creation/redemption procedures and related matters. “Permitted parties” in reviewed U.S. AP forms are typically additional entities allowed to act for an AP (such as affiliates or designees); they are not necessarily signatories themselves. The main signatories are generally the ETF trust, its adviser or distributor, and the AP. The trust is typically a Delaware statutory trust registered as an investment company under the 1940 Act—not a party exempt from that status because it is an ETF.

By contrast, an Irish ICAV arrangement is governed by its constitutional and contractual structure: the ICAV (or its management company) and the AP contract, with the depositary/custodian and administrator performing separate operational roles. Rule 6c-11 does not apply to the Irish ICAV.
